request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A hold now has dates, and a person can have several. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**Stored data**
- A new migration, `V28__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table with a from-date and an optional to-date, and drops the old `held` column.
- Anyone who was held before the change gets one hold with no start or end date, so their totals stay exactly as they were.

**Server**
- `PersonHold` is the new hold record. `Person` keeps a list of holds and has two checks: `isHeld()` (does the person have any hold) and `isHeldOn(date)` (does a date fall inside one of them).
- The hold endpoint now takes a from-date and a to-date. A blank from-date means the sheet's today; a blank to-date means the hold has no end.
- A hold whose to-date is before its from-date is refused.
- Each hold writes `PERSON_HELD … name=<name> from=<date>` to the audit file. When the hold changes the figures, the usual `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines follow.
- The release endpoint and the `PERSON_RELEASED` record are removed.
- The rule for what counts is updated in all three places that apply it: the live totals (`Rollup`), statements, and the period due-total worked out when a period is closed. An open claim is now left out only if its date falls within one of the person's holds and no statement binds it.

**Front end** (`people.ts`, `people-api.ts`)
- Each person's row shows "yes"/"no" for whether they have any hold, then lists each hold on its own line (`person-hold-line`).
- Below that are from-date and to-date fields and a Hold button. The Release button is gone.
- The totals on screen use the same rule as the server.
- Bad dates, or a to-date before the from-date, show the row's error (`person-error`). The error clears when either date field is edited or the next action is taken.

**Decisions for you**
- Pending claims count as open here, as they did before, so they're held too.
- A statement binds held claims that already carry a figure from an earlier statement again; held claims that were never bound stay unbound.
- Holds may overlap, and there's no way to delete one. The request says a hold simply ends on its to-date.
